akhfash:3-3.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلسَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِراً وَإِمَّا كَفُوراً ﴾; likewise ﴿إِمَّا ٱلعَذَابَ وَإِمَّا ٱلسَّاعَةَ﴾: it is as if you had not mentioned "إمَّا" ("either"); and if you wish, you begin afresh with what follows it and make it nominative.

akhfash:6-6.t: And He said ﴿عَيْناً يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ ٱللَّهِ﴾: He made it accusative in three ways. If you wish, it is on His words ﴿يَشْرَبُونَ﴾ [5] "﴿عَيْناً﴾" ("they drink … a spring"); if you wish, on ﴿يَشْرَبُونَ مِن كَأْسٍ كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا كَافُوراً﴾ ﴿عَيْناً﴾; and if you wish, by way of praise (madḥ), as when a man mentions someone to you and you say "العاقلَ واللبيبَ" ("the intelligent one, the discerning one!"), that is: you have mentioned the intelligent, discerning one — on the pattern "أَعْنِي عَيْناً" ("I mean a spring").

akhfash:9-9.t: [And He said] ﴿وَلاَ شُكُوراً﴾: if you wish, you make it the plural of "الشُكْر" (thanks), and make "الكُفُور" the plural of "الكُفْر" (ingratitude), like "الفَلْس" and "الفُلُوس". And if you wish, you make it a single maṣdar (verbal noun) with a plural meaning, like "قَعَد قُعُودا" and "خَرَج خُروجا".

akhfash:13-14.t: And He said ﴿مُّتَّكِئِينَ﴾: by way of praise (madḥ), or on "جَزَاهُمْ جَنَّةً مَتُكَّئِيِنَ فيها" ("He rewarded them with a garden, reclining in it") as a ḥāl (circumstantial). And you may say "جَزاَهُم ذلكَ قِياماً" ("He rewarded them with that, standing"). Likewise ﴿وَدَانِيَةً﴾ is a ḥāl or by way of praise; its accusative is only due to an implied verb. It is also permissible in His words ﴿وَدَانِيَةً﴾ for it to be on two aspects: on "وجزاهمْ دانيةً ظِلاَلُها" ("and He rewarded them with [a garden] whose shades are near"), as you say "اَعطَيْتُكَ جَيْداً طَرَفاهُ" ("I gave you one whose two ends are good") and "رأينَا حَسَناً وَجْهُهُ" ("we saw one whose face is handsome"). «[Translator's note: only one of the "two aspects" is spelled out in the source.]»

akhfash:17-17.t:
And He said ﴿كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنجَبِيلاً﴾: He made "the spring" (العين) accusative in four ways: on "يُسْقَوْنَ عَيْناً" ("they are given a spring to drink"), or as a ḥāl (circumstantial), or as a badal (substitute) for "the cup", or by way of praise (madḥ), the verb being implied. Some said that "سلسبيل" is a description (ṣifa) of the spring, describing it as salsabīl. And some said: "He only meant 'a spring that is named salsabīl' (عَيْناً تُسَمَّى سَلْسَبِيلاً)", that is: it is so called because of its excellence, that is: it is described (thus) to people, just as you say "الأعوجيّ" and "الأَرْحَبِيّ" and "المَهْرِيّ من الإِبل" (the Mahrī among camels); and just as horses, when described, are attributed to these well-known, pedigreed horses, so likewise the spring is attributed by being named [salsabīl], because the Qur'an points to the speech of the Arabs. The poet said — and Yūnus recited it to us thus — [in the kāmil metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-fourth verse cited as evidence]:
صَفْراءُ مِنْ نَبْعٍ يُسَمَّى سَهْمُها * مِنْ طُولِ ما صَرَعَ الصُّيُودَ الصَّيِّبُ
(A yellow [bow] of nabʿ wood, whose arrow is called — from how long it has felled the game — "the sure-hitter".)
He put "الصيِّب" in the nominative because he did not mean "its arrow is named 'the sure-hitter'" (يسمى سهمها بالصيِّب); rather "الصيِّب" is a description of the name and of the arrow. And his words "يسمى سهمها" mean: its arrow is spoken of. And some said: "No, rather it is the name of the spring, and it is definite; but since it is the end of a verse [and] it had fatḥa, you added the alif to it, as with ﴿قَوَارِيرَاْ﴾."

akhfash:20-20.t: And He said ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ نَعِيماً﴾: He means to make "رأَيْتَ" not take an object (intransitive), as one says "ظننت في الدار خيرٌ" ("I supposed: in the house there is good") on account of the place of his supposing; and He reported the place of his seeing.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿هَلْ أَتى﴾ an interrogative particle for arousing interest (tashwīq), and a past verb; and ﴿عَلَى الْإِنْسانِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿حِينٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent) of أتى; and ﴿مِنَ الدَّهْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of حين; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. And ﴿لَمْ يَكُنْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and its noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ khabar (predicate) of يكن; and ﴿مَذْكُوراً﴾ an adjective; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسانَ﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنا, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿أَمْشاجٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of نطفة; and ﴿نَبْتَلِيهِ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿سَمِيعاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿بَصِيراً﴾ an adjective; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿إِنَّا هَدَيْناهُ﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿السَّبِيلَ﴾ its second mafʿūl bihi; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنا, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position; and ﴿إِمَّا﴾ a particle of condition and detailing (sharṭ wa-tafṣīl); and ﴿شاكِراً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَإِمَّا كَفُوراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنا﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنا, and the nominal clause is resumptive; and ﴿لِلْكافِرِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿سَلاسِلَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَأَغْلالًا وَسَعِيراً﴾ both conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes them.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿إِنَّ الْأَبْرارَ يَشْرَبُونَ﴾ inna and its noun, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿مِنْ كَأْسٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive; and ﴿كانَ مِزاجُها كافُوراً﴾ kāna, its noun and its predicate; the clause is an adjective of كأس.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿عَيْناً﴾ badal (substitute) of كافورا; and ﴿يَشْرَبُ﴾ an imperfect verb; and ﴿بِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿عِبادُ اللَّهِ﴾ fāʿil (agent), annexed to the Name of Majesty; the verbal clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of عينا; and ﴿يُفَجِّرُونَها﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿تَفْجِيراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿يُوفُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿بِالنَّذْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is resumptive; and ﴿وَيَخافُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿يَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿كانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيراً﴾ kāna, its noun and its predicate; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of يوما.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وَيُطْعِمُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿الطَّعامَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿عَلى حُبِّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿مِسْكِيناً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿يَتِيماً وَأَسِيراً﴾ both conjoined to what precedes them.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿إِنَّما نُطْعِمُكُمْ﴾ restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa), and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the object of an implied saying (maqūl qawl muqaddar); and ﴿لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and ﴿لا﴾ negative; and ﴿نُرِيدُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿جَزاءً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَلا﴾ negative; and ﴿شُكُوراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جزاء.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿إِنَّا نَخافُ﴾ inna and its noun, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿مِنْ رَبِّنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿يَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿عَبُوساً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of يوما; and ﴿قَمْطَرِيراً﴾ a second adjective; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنا, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿فَوَقاهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the Name of Majesty is fāʿil (agent); and ﴿شَرَّ ذلِكَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, annexed to the demonstrative; and ﴿الْيَوْمِ﴾ badal (substitute) of the demonstrative; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَقَّاهُمْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to فوقاهم. ﴿نَضْرَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿سُرُوراً﴾ conjoined to نضرة.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿وَجَزاهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿بِما صَبَرُوا﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition, and mā is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya), and a past verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from mā and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the bāʾ, and the preposition [with its genitive noun] is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿جَنَّةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿حَرِيراً﴾ conjoined to جنة.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb); and ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; and ﴿عَلَى الْأَرائِكِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in متكئين. And ﴿لا﴾ negative; and ﴿يَرَوْنَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿شَمْساً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; and ﴿لا زَمْهَرِيراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to شمسا; the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿وَدانِيَةً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to متكئين; and ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) دانية; and ﴿ظِلالُها﴾ fāʿil (agent) of دانية; and ﴿وَذُلِّلَتْ﴾ a passive past verb; and ﴿قُطُوفُها﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and ﴿تَذْلِيلًا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to دانية.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿وَيُطافُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb; and ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿بِآنِيَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿مِنْ فِضَّةٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of آنية; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَأَكْوابٍ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كانَتْ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿قَوارِيرَا﴾ its khabar (predicate); the verbal clause is an adjective of أكواب.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿قَوارِيرَا﴾ badal (substitute) of what precedes it; and ﴿مِنْ فِضَّةٍ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of قوارير; and ﴿قَدَّرُوها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿تَقْدِيراً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿وَيُسْقَوْنَ﴾ a conjunction, and a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and ﴿فِيها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿كَأْساً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿كانَ مِزاجُها زَنْجَبِيلًا﴾ kāna, its noun and its predicate; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of كأسا.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿عَيْناً﴾ badal (substitute) of زنجبيلا; and ﴿فِيها﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of عينا; and ﴿تُسَمَّى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿سَلْسَبِيلًا﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a second adjective of عينا.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وَيَطُوفُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); and ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿وِلْدانٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent); and ﴿مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of ولدان; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. And ﴿إِذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive; and ﴿رَأَيْتَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation; and ﴿حَسِبْتَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿لُؤْلُؤاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿مَنْثُوراً﴾ an adjective of لؤلؤا; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:20-20.t: ﴿وَإِذا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction; and ﴿إِذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive; and ﴿رَأَيْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation; and ﴿ثَمَّ﴾ an adverb of place; and ﴿رَأَيْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿نَعِيماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَمُلْكاً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to نعيما; and ﴿كَبِيراً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿عالِيَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); and ﴿ثِيابُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), annexed to ﴿سُندُسٍ﴾; and ﴿خُضْرٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of ثياب; the nominal clause is resumptive; and ﴿إِسْتَبْرَقٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ثياب. ﴿وَحُلُّوا﴾ the wāw is of ḥāl (circumstantial), and a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and ﴿أَساوِرَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿مِنْ فِضَّةٍ﴾ an adjective of أساور; the clause is a ḥāl clause. ﴿وَسَقاهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿رَبُّهُمْ﴾ fāʿil (agent); and ﴿شَراباً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿طَهُوراً﴾ an adjective of شرابا; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿إِنَّ هذا كانَ﴾ inna and its noun, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿لَكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿جَزاءً﴾ khabar; the clause of kāna is the khabar of inna, and the clause is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl qawl maḥdhūf). ﴿وَكانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُوراً﴾ kāna, its noun and its predicate; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun; and ﴿نَحْنُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); and ﴿نَزَّلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنا, and the nominal clause is resumptive; and ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿الْقُرْآنَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿تَنْزِيلًا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿لِحُكْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. And ﴿وَلا تُطِعْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lā, whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿آثِماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction; and ﴿كَفُوراً﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to آثما; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:25-25.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرِ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿اسْمَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed to ﴿رَبِّكَ﴾, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بُكْرَةً﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿وَأَصِيلًا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to بكرة; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:26-26.t: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) اسجد; and ﴿فَاسْجُدْ﴾ the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿وَسَبِّحْهُ﴾ an imperative verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿لَيْلًا﴾ an adverb of time; and ﴿طَوِيلًا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa).

daas-irab:27-27.t: ﴿إِنَّ هؤُلاءِ يُحِبُّونَ﴾ inna and its noun, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿الْعاجِلَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl). ﴿وَيَذَرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿وَراءَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place; and ﴿يَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿ثَقِيلًا﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of يوما; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:28-28.t: ﴿نَحْنُ خَلَقْناهُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), and a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَشَدَدْنا أَسْرَهُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَإِذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive; and ﴿شِئْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation; and ﴿بَدَّلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿أَمْثالَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿تَبْدِيلًا﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:29-29.t: Its i'rab has preceded in verse 19 of Sūrat al-Muzzammil.

daas-irab:30-30.t: ﴿وَما﴾ negative; and ﴿تَشاؤُنَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the Name of Majesty is the fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation to an omitted adverb, i.e. «except at the time of Allah's willing»; and ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ﴾ inna and its noun, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿عَلِيماً حَكِيماً﴾ two predicates (khabar); the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīliyya).

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿يُدْخِلُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿فِي رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of من. ﴿وَالظَّالِمِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being «He punishes» (يعذب); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿أَعَدَّ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿عَذاباً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿أَلِيماً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is explicative (mufassira) of what precedes it.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿هَلْ أَتَىٰ عَلَى ٱلإِنسَانِ حِينٌ مِّنَ ٱلدَّهْرِ﴾.
Its meaning: there has indeed (قد) come upon man a period of time. "هل" may be a denial (jaḥd), and it may be a statement (khabar).
This is of the statement kind; because you may say: "Did I not admonish you (فهل وعظتك)? Did I not give you (فهل أعطيتك)?", making him affirm that you did give him and admonish him. The denial is when you say: "And can anyone (وهل يقدر واحد) do the like of this?"
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿لَمْ يَكُن شَيْئاً مَّذْكُوراً﴾.
He means: he was a thing, but he was not something mentioned. That is from the time Allah created him from clay until He breathed the spirit into him.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمْشَاجٍ نَّبْتَلِيهِ﴾.
الأمشاج: the mixtures — the man's fluid, the woman's fluid, the blood and the clot. When something of this sort [117/b] is mixed it is called مشيج, as you say خليط (mixed), and ممشوج, as you say مخلوط (mixed).
His saying: ﴿نَّبْتَلِيهِ﴾ — the meaning, and Allah knows best, is: We made him hearing and seeing in order to test him. This is placed earlier while its meaning is later; the meaning is only: We created him and made him hearing and seeing in order to test him.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ ٱلسَّبِيلَ﴾.
Also إلى السبيل and للسبيل; all of that is permissible in the speech of the Arabs. He says: We guided him, i.e. We made the way known to him, whether he is grateful or ungrateful. (إما) here may be conditional (jazāʾ), i.e.: whether he is grateful or whether he is ungrateful; or it may be the (إما) found in His saying: ﴿إِما يُعَذِّبُهُمْ وَإِمَّا يَتُوبُ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, as though He said: We created him wretched or happy.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَلاَسِلَ وَأَغْلاَلاً﴾.
"سلاسل" was written with an alif, and some of the readers declined it as a triptote (ajrāhā) because of the alif at its end, while some did not. The one who did not decline it said: the Arabs keep the alif in the accusative of what is a diptote (lā yujrā), and when they join it to what follows they drop the alif; and both are correct. Similar to that is His saying: ﴿كانَتْ قَوَارِيراً﴾ (15): the alif was kept in the first because it is the end of a verse, while the other is not [the end of] a verse. So keeping the alif in the first was stronger because of this argument, and that is how I saw it in the codex of ʿAbdullāh; the people of Basra read it so and wrote it so in their codices. The people of Kufa and Medina keep the alif in both of them together, as though they found it strange for one word with one accusative meaning to be written in two different ways. If you wish, you decline both as triptotes; if you wish, you decline neither; and if you wish, you decline the first because of the alif in the writing of the people of Basra and do not decline the second, since it has no alif.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَشْرَبُونَ مِن كَأْسٍ كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا كَافُوراً﴾.
It is said that it is a spring called al-Kāfūr. It may also be that its mixture is like camphor because of the fragrance of its scent, in which case it is not a name. The Arabs [118/a] put the accusative on whichever of these two words they like. Ḥassān said:
كأنَّ خبيئَةً من بيت رأْسٍ * يكونُ مِزاجُها عَسلٌ وماءُ
(As though a hidden [wine] from Bayt Raʾs, whose mixture is honey and water.)
It is clearer in meaning to make the verb [i.e. its accusative predicate] fall on المزاج, even though it is definite; and all is correct. You say: كان سيدَهم أبوك (your father was their chief) and كان سيدُهم أباك. The preferred way is to say: كان سيدَهم أبوك; because "father" is a fixed noun, whereas "chief" is one of the attributes.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَيْناً﴾.
If you wish, you make it follow الكافور as an explicative of it; and if you wish, you put it in the accusative by detachment (qaṭʿ) from the hāʾ in "مزاجها".
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَشْرَبُ بِهَا﴾, and "يَشْرَبُهَا".
They are the same in meaning. It is as though يشرب بها means: quenches his thirst with it and slakes it. As for يشربونها, it is clear. Someone recited to me:
شَرِبْنَ بِمَاءِ البحرِ ثمَّ تَرَفَّعتْ * مَتى لُججٍ خُضْرٍ لَهُنَّ نئيجُ
(They drank of the sea's water, then rose up out of green deep waves, with a roaring sound.)
Similar to it is: إنه ليتكلم بكلام حسن, and يتكلم كلاماً حسناً (he speaks with fine speech / he speaks fine speech).
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيراً﴾.
Whichever [place] a man of the people of Paradise likes, he makes it gush forth for himself.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُوفُونَ بِٱلنَّذْرِ﴾.
This is one of their attributes in this world; it is as though there is an implied كان in it: they used to fulfil the vow.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَخَافُونَ يَوْماً كَانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيراً﴾.
Its trial is far-spreading. The Arabs say: the crack spread (استطار) in the glass flask and the like, and also استطال.

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَبُوساً قَمْطَرِيراً﴾.
القمطرير: the severe. One says: يوم قمطرير and يوم قماطر (a severe day). Someone recited to me:
بَنِى عمِّنا، هل تذكُرونَ بَلاءَنا * علَيكُمْ إذا ما كانَ قُمَاطِرُ
(O sons of our uncle, do you remember our good service to you when there was a severe [day]?)

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He [«عز وجلك» in the source — Translator's note: a typo for «عز وجل:»]: ﴿مُّتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا﴾.
It is in the accusative as by detachment (qaṭʿ). If you wish, you make it follow الجنة, as though you said: their reward is a Garden, reclining in it.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيْهِمْ ظِلاَلُهَا﴾.
It may be accusative on that [same pattern]: their reward is a Garden, reclining in it, and its shades being near. If you wish, you make الدانية follow المتكئين by way of detachment (qaṭʿ), which may also be nominative on [118/b] resumption (istiʾnāf). So it is permissible like His saying: ﴿وَهَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخاً﴾ and "وشيخٌ". In the reading of Ubayy it is: "ودانٍ عليهم ظلالها", and this is resumptive, in the position of the nominative; and in the reading of ʿAbdullāh: "ودانياً عليهم ظلالها". The masculine and feminine forms of الداني are like His saying: ﴿خَاشِعاً أبْصَارُهم﴾ in one place and ﴿خاشعةً أبصارهم﴾ in another. الدانية may also be accusative on the pattern of the Arabs' saying: عند فلان جاريةٌ جميلةٌ، وشابةً بعدُ طريةً (So-and-so has a beautiful slave-girl, and young still, fresh), interposing praise parenthetically, without intending it to be coordinated with what precedes; it is as though they imply with this wāw a verb by which the accusative comes about, [as] in one of the two readings: "وحوراً عيناً". Someone recited to me:
ويأوى إلى نسوة عاطلاتٍ * وشُعثا مراضيعَ مثل السعالِى
(And he takes refuge with women bare of ornament, and dishevelled ones, nursing mothers, like ghouls.)
with the accusative, i.e.: وشعثا; though the genitive is more common.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُهَا تَذْلِيلاً﴾.
The people of Paradise pick the fruit standing and sitting, and in every state, with no effort in it.

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَانَتْ قَوَارِيرَاْ﴾.
He says: they had the clarity of glass and the whiteness of silver, so the clarity of glass and the whiteness of silver were combined in them.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدَّرُوهَا﴾.
They measured the cup to the thirst of each one of them, with nothing left over and nothing falling short of quenching his thirst; and that is the most delightful drink.
Some have transmitted from al-Shaʿbī: (قُدِّروها تَقْدِيراً). The meaning is the same, and Allah knows best: "it was measured for them" and "they measured it" are equivalent.

farraa:17-18.t:
His saying: ﴿كَأْساً كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنجَبِيلاً﴾.
It is only called a كأس when there is drink in it; when there is no wine in it, the name كأس does not apply to it.
I heard one of the Arabs say of the tray on which a gift is presented: it is the مِهْدَى, as long as the gift is on it; when it is [119/a] empty it reverts to its own name, whether it is a tray (طبق) or a table (خوان) or something else.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿زَنجَبِيلاً عَيْناً﴾.
It is mentioned that the ginger (الزنجبيل) is the spring, and that الزنجبيل is a name for it; and the same interpretation applies to it as to الكافور.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تُسَمَّىٰ سَلْسَبِيلاً﴾.
They mentioned that السلسبيل is a name for the spring, and it is mentioned that it is a description of the water for its smooth flowing and its sweetness. We consider that if it were a name for the spring, leaving it undeclined (tark al-ijrāʾ, i.e. treating it as a diptote) would be more common; yet we have not seen any of the readers leave it undeclined, though that is permissible in Arabic, just as in the reading of ʿAbdullāh: ﴿وَلاَ تَذَرُنّ وَدًّا ولا سُوَاعاً ولا يَغُوثاً ويَعُوقاً﴾ with the alif, and as they said "سلاسلا" and "قواريرا" with the alif, declining as triptotes what is not declined. That is not a mistake, because the Arabs decline as triptotes in poetry what is not declined; if it were a mistake they would not have brought it into their poems. Mutammim ibn Nuwayra said:
فما وجد أظآرٍ ثلاثٍ روائمٍ * رأين مَجَرًّا من حُوارٍ ومصْرعَا
(The grief of three foster she-camels, tenderly attached, that saw where a young camel was dragged and where it fell, is not [like mine].)
So he declined روائم as a triptote, though it is one of those not declined — [this occurs] in more instances than I can count in their poems.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مُّخَلَّدُونَ﴾.
He says: adorned and wearing bracelets; it is also said: wearing earrings; and it is said: مخلدون means their youth is everlasting, they do not change from that age. This is the most likely to be correct — and Allah knows best — because when a man grows old among the Arabs and the blackness of his hair remains, it is said: إنه لمخلد. Likewise, when he grows old and his teeth and molars remain [firm], it is said: إنه لمخلد, i.e. of unchanging condition.
Likewise the youths: their teeth remain [unchanged].

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ نَعِيماً﴾.
It is said: when you see what is there (ما ثَمّ), you see bliss; and implying (ما) is acceptable, just as it was said: ﴿لَقَدْ تَقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾, the meaning being: what is between you, and Allah knows best. It is also said: إذا رأيت [119/b] ثم, meaning: when you look; then when you cast your sight there you see bliss.

farraa:21-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿عَالِيَهُمْ ثِيَابُ سُندُسٍ﴾.
Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, ʿĀṣim and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī read it in the accusative, treating it like an adverb: "above them". The Arabs say: قومك داخلَ الدار (your people are inside the house), putting داخل الدار in the accusative because it is a place (maḥall); and عاليهم is of that kind. The people of the Hijaz and Ḥamza read: "عَالِيهم" with the yāʾ left unvowelled (irsāl), and in the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is: "عاليتُهم ثيابُ سُنْدُسٍ" with tāʾ — and that is an argument for whoever leaves the yāʾ unvowelled and makes it quiescent. The readers differed over الخضر and السندس [Translator's note: so in the source; the context indicates خضر and إستبرق]: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb put them both in the genitive, intending to make الخضر a description of السندس and ويكسر على الاستبرق [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently "and to make الاستبرق coordinate with it"] — ثيابُ سندس and ثيابُ استبرق. Al-Ḥasan put both words in the nominative, making الخضر a description of الثياب and putting الاستبرق in the nominative by coordinating it back onto الثياب. Some put الخضر in the nominative and الاستبرق in the genitive, and [others] put الاستبرق in the nominative and الخضر in the genitive; and all of that is correct. And Allah is praised.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿شَرَاباً طَهُوراً﴾.
He says: pure, not impure, as it [wine] was spoken of as impure in this world.

farraa:24-24.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ آثِماً أَوْ كَفُوراً ﴾.
(وُ) [Translator's note: so in the source; read (أو)] here is equivalent to (لا). أو, in denial, interrogation and conditional (jazāʾ) [contexts], has the meaning of (لا), and this is one of those. The poet said:
لا وَجْدُ ثَكْلَى كما وَجِدْتُ وَلا * وَجْدُ عَجُولٍ أَضَلَّهَا رُبَعُ
أَوْ وَجْدُ شيخٍ أصَلَّ ناقَتهُ * يَوْمَ توافَى الحجيجُ فاندفعُوا
(Neither the grief of a bereaved mother is like the grief I felt, nor the grief of a she-camel that lost her young calf, or the grief of an old man who lost his she-camel on the day the pilgrims gathered and then pushed on.)
He meant: ولا وجد شيخ (nor the grief of an old man). In Arabic it may also be: do not obey among them anyone who sins or disbelieves.
Then the meaning of (أو) is close to the meaning of (الواو), as when you say to a man: لأعطينك سألت أو سكتّ (I will surely give to you, whether you ask or keep silent), meaning: I will surely give to you in any case.

farraa:28-28.t:
His saying [120/a], Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَشَدَدْنَآ أَسْرَهُمْ﴾.
الأسر: the make (الخلق). You say: لقد أُسِر هذا الرجل أحسنَ الأسر (this man has been made with the finest make), as you say: خُلِقَ أحسنَ الخَلْق (he was created with the finest creation).

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾.
He says: this sura is a reminder and an admonition. ﴿فَمَن شَآءَ ٱتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلاً﴾: a direction and a road to good.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ﴾.
A response to His saying: ﴿فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتّخذَ إلَى رَبِّهِ سَبِيلاً﴾.
Then He informed them that the matter is not up to them, and said: ﴿وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ﴾ that way ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ for you. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh: ﴿وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, identical to the standard reading; the following remark suggests ʿAbdullāh's reading had (ما) in place of (أن), i.e. «إلا ما شاء الله»]. The meaning of (ما) and (أن) is close.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلظَّالِمِينَ أَعَدَّ لَهُمْ﴾.
You put الظالمين in the accusative because the wāw in لها [Translator's note: so in the source; apparently "the lām in لهم" is meant] becomes like an adverbial container (ẓarf) for أعدّ. If it were nominative it would be correct, as He said: ﴿والشُّعَرَاءُ يَتَّبِعُهُمُ الْغَاوُونَ﴾ without hamza. In the reading of ʿAbdullāh it is: "وللظالمين أعد لهم", repeating the lām in (الظالمين) and in (لهم); and the Arabs sometimes do that. Someone recited to me:
أقول لها إذا سألت طلاقا * إلامَ تسارعين إلى فراقى
(I say to her, when she asks for divorce: to what end do you hasten to part from me?)
And someone recited to me:
فأصبحْنَ لا يَسلنهُ عن بما به * أصعَّد فى غاوى الهَوى أم تصوَّبا؟
(And by morning they would not ask him about what was with him: had he gone up in the error of passion, or come down?)
So he repeated the bāʾ twice [Translator's note: in the verse what is repeated is the preposition عن with ب]. Had he said: لا يسلنه عما به, it would have been clearer and better; but the poet sometimes adds and omits to complete the verse. If you directed the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ، عن النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيم﴾ to this interpretation, it would be correct in Arabic.
It has another interpretation, meaning: About what are they asking one another, O Muhammad! Then He informed and said: they are asking one another about the great news. Similar to this is His saying in al-Mursalāt: ﴿لأَِىِّ يَوْمٍ أُجِّلَتْ﴾ as an expression of wonder, then He said: ﴿ليوم الفصل﴾, i.e.: they were deferred to the Day of Decision.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Insān
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿هَلْ أتى عَلى الإنْسانِ حِينٌ مِنَ الدَّهْرِ لَمْ يَكُنْ شَيْئًا مَذْكُورًا﴾: the meaning is: "Has there not come upon man a period of time when he was already something" — except that he was dust and clay until the spirit was breathed into him? — "so before the spirit was breathed into him he was not a thing mentioned." It is also possible that all people are meant by it, the meaning being that they were drops of sperm, then clinging clots, then lumps of flesh, until they became a thing mentioned. The meaning of ﴿هَلْ أتى﴾ is "there has indeed come upon man", that is: "Has there not come upon man a period of time…?"

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying: ﴿إنّا خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ مِن نُطْفَةٍ أمْشاجٍ نَبْتَلِيهِ﴾: «أمْشاجٍ» means mixtures — sperm and blood — then he is moved from one state to another. The singular of الأمْشاج is «مَشَجٌ». The meaning of «نَبْتَلِيهِ» is: We test him. What points to this is: ﴿فَجَعَلْناهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا﴾, that is: "We made him so in order to test him."

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿إنّا هَدَيْناهُ السَّبِيلَ إمّا شاكِرًا وإمّا كَفُورًا﴾: its meaning is: We guided him to the way, whether to wretchedness or to felicity.

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿سَلاسِلَ وأغْلالا وسَعِيرًا﴾: the best usage in Arabic is that «سَلاسِلَ» not be declined as a triptote (i.e. that it be treated as a diptote), but since it was made the end of a verse it was given nunation, so that the ends of the verses would be on one pattern.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّ الأبْرارَ يَشْرَبُونَ مِن كَأْسٍ﴾: «اَلْأبْرارُ», its singular is «بَرٌّ». ﴿يَشْرَبُونَ مِن كَأْسٍ كانَ مِزاجُها كافُورًا﴾: linguistically it may be that the taste of fragrance and of camphor is in it, and it is possible that it is mixed with camphor without any harm in that, because the people of the Garden are touched by no harm and no fatigue in what they eat and drink. «اَلْكَأْسُ» in the language is the vessel when there is drink in it; when there is no drink in it, it is not called a كَأْس. The poet said:
؎صَدَدْتِ الكَأْسَ عَنّا أُمَّ عَمْرٍو ∗∗∗ وكانَ الكَأْسُ مَجْراها اليَمِينا
(You turned the cup away from us, O Umm ʿAmr, though the cup's course was to pass to the right.)

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِها عِبادُ اللَّهِ﴾: «عَيْنًا» may be part of the description of the cup, but the better view is that the meaning is "from a spring". His saying: ﴿يُفَجِّرُونَها تَفْجِيرًا﴾ means: "that spring flows for them as they wish."

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿كانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيرًا﴾: its meaning is: it reaches the utmost extent.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعامَ عَلى حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا﴾: this hāʾ (pronoun) refers back to the food. The meaning is: they give food to the poor man when their own need for it is at its most severe; and Allah described them as preferring others over themselves. ﴿وَيَتِيمًا وأسِيرًا﴾: «اَلْأسِيرُ» (the captive) — it was said that at that time he was one of the unbelievers. And whoever feeds a captive was praised, though he is an unbeliever — so how much more the Muslim captives! This indicates that in feeding those held in prisons there is abundant reward, and the people of the prisons are captives.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّما نُطْعِمُكم لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ لا نُرِيدُ مِنكم جَزاءً ولا شُكُورًا﴾: the meaning is "saying: We feed you only for the countenance of Allah", that is: seeking the reward of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is possible that they fed without uttering these words, but this was their intention in feeding, so what was in their hearts was expressed in words. Likewise: ﴿إنّا نَخافُ مِن رَبِّنا يَوْمًا عَبُوسًا قَمْطَرِيرًا﴾ [al-Insān: 10]. «اَلْعُبُوسُ» is that which makes faces frown; this is like His saying: ﴿وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ باسِرَةٌ﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 24]. As for «قَمْطَرِيرًا», one says «يَوْمٌ قَمْطَرِيرٌ» and «يَوْمٌ قُماطِرٌ» when it is severe and harsh. It has come in the exegesis that «قَمْطَرِيرًا» means: it frowns so that what is between the eyes is drawn together; and this is acceptable in the language: one says «اِقْمَطَرَّتِ النّاقَةُ» when the she-camel raises her tail, draws her flanks together and thrusts out her nose.

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيها عَلى الأرائِكِ﴾: its singular is «أرِيكَةٌ». It has come in the exegesis that they are of the curtained canopies containing bedding and couches; and in the language every thing reclined upon is an «أرِيكَةٌ». ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ﴾ is in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "and He rewarded them with a Garden while they are reclining in it." Likewise: ﴿وَدانِيَةً عَلَيْهِمْ ظِلالُها وذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُها تَذْلِيلا﴾ [al-Insān: 14]. It is also possible that «دانِيَةً» is a naʿt (adjective) of the Garden; the meaning is: "and He rewarded them with a Garden whose shades are close over them."

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُها تَذْلِيلا﴾: this is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿قُطُوفُها دانِيَةٌ﴾ [al-Ḥāqqa: 23]. It was said: whenever they want to pick something of it, it is made easy for them and comes near to them, whether they are sitting, lying down or standing.

zajjaj:15-15.t: ﴿وَيُطافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِآنِيَةٍ مِن فِضَّةٍ وأكْوابٍ كانَتْ قَوارِيرا﴾ ﴿قَوارِيرا﴾ [al-Insān: 16]: it was read without nunation (as a diptote), and this is the preferred choice of the Basran grammarians, because every plural that has two letters after its alif is diptote; we have explained this earlier in the book. Whoever read «قَوارِيرًا», giving nunation to the first, did so because it is the end of a verse, and left the second without nunation because it is not the end of a verse. Whoever gave nunation to the second made the word follow the word, because the Arabs sometimes alter the case-ending of a thing so that the word follows the word, saying «هَذا جُحْرُ ضَبٍّ خَرِبٍ» ("this is a ruined lizard's hole"), whereas خَرِب is really the adjective of the hole — so how much more with what is left undeclined! And everything that is left undeclined may be given nunation in poetry.

zajjaj:16-16.t: The meaning of ﴿قَوارِيرا مِن فِضَّةٍ قَدَّرُوها تَقْدِيرًا﴾: the origin of the glass vessels (qawārīr) of this world is from sand, so Allah made known that the excellence of those vessels is that their origin is of silver, what is inside them being seen from their outside. The meaning of ﴿قَدَّرُوها تَقْدِيرًا﴾ is: they were made such that the vessel is according to the measure of what they need and want. It was also read «قُدِّرُوها تَقْدِيرًا», that is: they were made for them according to the measure of their wish.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
﴿وَيُسْقَوْنَ فِيها كَأْسًا كانَ مِزاجُها زَنْجَبِيلا﴾, that is: it combines the taste of ginger. The Arabs describe ginger, and it is very much relished by them. The poet said:
؎كَأنَّ القَرَنْفُلَ والزَّنْجَبِيلَ ∗∗∗ باتا بِفِيها وأرْيًا مَشُورا
(As though cloves and ginger had spent the night in her mouth, and gathered honey.)
So it may be that the taste of ginger is in it, and it may be that ginger is its mixture without any ill effect from it, as we said regarding camphor.

zajjaj:18-18.t: His saying: ﴿عَيْنًا فِيها تُسَمّى سَلْسَبِيلا﴾: the meaning is "they are given to drink from a spring". «سَلْسَبِيلُ» is the name of the spring, except that it was given nunation because it is the end of a verse. «سَلْسَبِيلُ» in the language is a description of whatever is extremely smooth-flowing, so it is as though the spring — and Allah knows best — was named by its description.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
﴿وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾, that is: youthful servants, made everlasting, serve them. The interpretation of ﴿مُخَلَّدُونَ﴾ is: none of them ever passes beyond the age of youthful service; he remains a youthful servant. The Arabs say of a man who does not grow grey: «هُوَ مُخَلَّدٌ». It is also said that «مُخَلَّدُونَ» means: adorned, wearing ornaments; and a set of ornaments is called «اَلْخَلَدَةُ».
His saying: ﴿حَسِبْتَهم لُؤْلُؤًا مَنثُورًا﴾, that is: in the beauty and purity of their colours they are like scattered pearls.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿وَإذا رَأيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأيْتَ نَعِيمًا ومُلْكًا كَبِيرًا﴾: it has come in the exegesis that «مُلْكًا كَبِيرًا» means that the angels greet them with peace; and it has also come: the angels ask their permission to enter. «ثَمَّ» (there) refers to the Garden. What governs (al-ʿāmil) «ثَمَّ» is the meaning of «رَأيْتَ»; the meaning is: "and when you see with your sight there". It was also said that the meaning is: "and when you see what is there, you see bliss", but this is a mistake, because on this interpretation «ما» would be a relative noun whose ṣila (relative clause) is «ثَمَّ», and it is not permissible to drop the relative noun and leave its ṣila. Rather, «رَأيْتَ» extends in meaning to «ثَمَّ».

zajjaj:21-21.t:
His saying: «عالِيهِمْ ثِيابُ سُنْدُسٍ», with the yāʾ unvowelled; it was also read ﴿عالِيَهُمْ﴾ with the yāʾ vowelled with fatḥa, and it was read «عَلَيْهِمْ» without alif, ﴿ثِيابُ سُنْدُسٍ﴾. These three agree with the written codex (al-muṣḥaf), and all of them are good in Arabic. It was also read in two ways other than these three: it was read «عالِيَتُهم ثِيابُ سُنْدُسٍ» in the nominative and the feminine, and «عالِيَتَهُمْ» in the accusative. These two ways are good in Arabic, except that they differ from the codex, and I do not consider reading with them acceptable; the readers of the great cities do not read with them.
As for the explanation of the unvowelled «عالِيهِمْ», with the yāʾ unvowelled: it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is ﴿ثِيابُ سُنْدُسٍ خُضْرٌ﴾. As for whoever put it in the accusative and said ﴿عالِيَهُمْ﴾ with fatḥa on the yāʾ, one of the grammarians said that he makes it accusative as an adverb of place (ẓarf), as you say «فَوْقَهم ثِيابٌ» ("above them are garments"). But we do not know this among the adverbs; and if it were an adverb, it would not be permissible to make the yāʾ unvowelled. Rather, its accusative is as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from one of two things. One of them is from the hāʾ and mīm (-hum); the meaning is: "youthful servants made everlasting go round among the righteous, garments of fine silk being upon the righteous" — because He has described their states in the Garden, so the meaning is: "these go round among them in this state." It may also be a ḥāl from the youthful servants; the meaning is: "when you see them you would think them scattered pearls, in the state of the garments being over them." So the accusative on this account is clear.
As for «عَلَيْهِمْ ثِيابُ سُنْدُسٍ», it is nominative, as when you say «عَلَيْكَ مالٌ» ("you owe money"): you put it in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the meaning is: "and garments of fine silk are upon them." The explanation of the accusative and nominative of «عالِيَتَهُمْ» is like the explanation of «عالِيَهُمْ».
«اَلسُّنْدُسُ» is silk. It was read «خُضْرٌ» and «خُضْرٍ». Whoever read «خُضْرٌ» — and this is better — makes it a naʿt (adjective) of the garments, since the word الثِّياب is a plural word and «خُضْرٌ» is a plural word. Whoever read «خُضْرٍ» makes it an adjective of السُّنْدُس, and «اَلسُّنْدُسُ» in meaning refers back to the garments.
It was read «وَإسْتَبْرَقٌ» — which is thick, heavy, coarse brocade — and it was read in the nominative and in the genitive. Whoever put it in the nominative conjoined it to «ثِيابُ»; the meaning is: "upon them is brocade (إسْتَبْرَقٌ)." Whoever put it in the genitive conjoined it to السُّنْدُس, and the meaning is: "upon them are garments of these two kinds, garments of fine silk and brocade."
It was also read «وَإسْتَبْرَقَ» in two ways other than these two, both of them very weak in Arabic. It was read «وَإسْتَبْرَقَ وحُلُّوا», with إسْتَبْرَقَ in the accusative form while it is in a genitive position, not given nunation; Ibn Muḥayṣin read it so. They claimed that he did not give it nunation because «وَإسْتَبْرَقَ» is a foreign noun, its origin in Persian being «اِسْتَبْرَهُ», so when it was transferred into Arabic it was not declined. This is a mistake, because it is indefinite — do you not see that the alif and lām enter it? You say: «اَلسُّنْدُسُ والإسْتَبْرَقُ». The second way is «واسْتَبْرَقَ وحُلُّوا», dropping the alif: he made the alif a connective alif (alif al-waṣl) and made it something named with the verb derived from al-barīq (gleaming). This is an error, because الإسْتَبْرَق is known — it is well known that it is a noun transferred from Persian into Arabic, just as الدِّيباج (brocade) was named, which is likewise transferred from Persian.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَسَقاهم رَبُّهم شَرابًا طَهُورًا﴾: it has come in the exegesis that when they drink it their bellies become lean and their skins exude sweat like the scent of musk. It was also said that it is pure, not filth like the wine of this world.

zajjaj:24-24.t: His saying: ﴿وَلا تُطِعْ مِنهم آثِمًا أوْ كَفُورًا﴾: «أوْ» here is more emphatic than the wāw. For with the wāw, if you say «لا تُطِعْ زَيْدًا وعَمْرًا» ("do not obey Zayd and ʿAmr") and he obeys one of the two, he is not disobedient, because he commanded him not to obey the two together. But when He said ﴿وَلا تُطِعْ مِنهم آثِمًا أوْ كَفُورًا﴾, «أوْ» indicated that each one of them deserves to be disobeyed. Likewise, when you say «لا تُخالِفِ الحَسَنَ أوِ ابْنَ سِيرِينَ» ("do not oppose al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn") or «اِتَّبِعِ الحَسَنَ أوِ ابْنَ سِيرِينَ» ("follow al-Ḥasan or Ibn Sīrīn"), you have said: "These two deserve to be followed," and each one of them is deserving. We have given the like of this explanation for a word other than this one at the beginning of Sūrat al-Baqara, in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿مَثَلُهم كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي اسْتَوْقَدَ نارًا﴾ [al-Baqara: 17] to the end of the verse, and after that ﴿أوْ كَصَيِّبٍ مِنَ السَّماءِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 19], whose interpretation is the same: for whether you liken them to the one who kindled a fire, or liken them to the rainstorm, or to both together, you are correct.

zajjaj:25-25.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿واذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ بُكْرَةً وأصِيلا﴾: «اَلْأصِيلُ» is the late afternoon/evening (al-ʿashiyy). One says «قَدْ أصَلْنا» ("we have entered the aṣīl") when they enter the aṣīl, which is the ʿashiyy.

zajjaj:28-28.t: His saying: ﴿نَحْنُ خَلَقْناهم وشَدَدْنا أسْرَهُمْ﴾: «أسْرَهُمْ» means their make (khalq). It has also come in the exegesis: their joints.

zajjaj:30-30.t: His saying: ﴿وَما تَشاءُونَ إلا أنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ إنَّ اللَّهَ كانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا﴾, that is: you do not will except by the will of Allah.

zajjaj:31-31.t: ﴿والظّالِمِينَ أعَدَّ لَهم عَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾: «الظّالِمِينَ» is in the accusative because what precedes it is accusative. The meaning is: "He admits whom He wills into His mercy, and He punishes the wrongdoers — He has prepared for them a painful punishment," and ﴿أعَدَّ لَهُمْ﴾ is an explanation (tafsīr) of this implied (muḍmar) verb. It was also read «والظّالِمُونَ», but I do not consider reading with it acceptable, for two reasons. One of them is that it differs from the codex. The other is that, even if it is permissible in Arabic — on the basis that «اَلظّالِمِينَ» is put in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what comes after «اَلظّالِمِينَ» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ — the preferred choice of the Basran grammarians is the accusative. The grammarians say: «أعْطَيْتُ زَيْدًا وعَمْرًا أعَدَدْتُ لَهُ بُرًّا» ("I gave to Zayd, and ʿAmr — I prepared wheat for him"), and they prefer the accusative in the sense of "and I treated ʿAmr kindly", and «أبَرُّ عَمْرًا أعْدَدْتُ لَهُ بُرًّا». So they choose for the Qur'an nothing but the best of the ways — and this, moreover, in agreement with the codex.
